subject: Tom Jackson
title: Tom Jackson ESPN: Broncos great and NFL analyst dies at 75
answer: Tom Jackson, the Denver Broncos linebacker who spent nearly three decades as an NFL studio analyst at ESPN, died Friday, Nov. 20, 2026, at age 75. Longtime partner Chris Berman announced the news on ESPN's "Sunday NFL Countdown" on Nov. 22. No cause of death has been disclosed.
in_the_news: Jackson's family asked that the news wait until the start of Sunday's "Countdown," the show he helped build, so many fans learned of it live on air. ESPN's NFL studio in Bristol, Connecticut, still carries his name alongside Berman's.
body:
Jackson's family informed ESPN of his death, and Berman delivered it on air as the "Countdown" crew wore orange ties in his honor. Berman, who called Jackson his best friend, described the death as unexpected and said the two had spoken earlier in the week. ESPN chairman Jimmy Pitaro called Jackson one of the most influential and beloved figures in the network's history. The Broncos said he had been a cherished member of the franchise's family for more than 50 years. Jackson is survived by his wife, Jennifer, and daughters Taylor and Morgan.

On the field, Jackson was a fourth-round pick out of Louisville in 1973 and played all 14 of his NFL seasons in Denver, through 1986. He was a leader of the "Orange Crush" defense that carried the Broncos to their first Super Bowl after the 1977 season, made three Pro Bowls (1977-79) and was a two-time All-Pro, according to AP. His 20 interceptions are tied with Randy Gradishar for the most by a Broncos linebacker, and his seven in 1976 remain the team's single-season record for the position. He retired at 36 after Denver reached Super Bowl XXI, and entered the Broncos Ring of Fame in 1992.

Jackson's career at a glance: 1973, drafted in the fourth round by Denver. 1977 season, starts on the Broncos' first Super Bowl team. 1986 season, retires after Super Bowl XXI. 1987, joins ESPN and pairs with Berman on "NFL PrimeTime" and later "Sunday NFL Countdown." 1992, inducted into the Broncos Ring of Fame. 2015, receives the Pro Football Hall of Fame's Pete Rozelle Radio-Television Award, five years after Berman. 2016, retires from ESPN; his last assignment was the Hall of Fame enshrinement in August.

Why he mattered to viewers: before highlights lived on phones, Sunday-night "PrimeTime" was where many fans first saw the day's plays, and Jackson's job was to explain them from a player's point of view. Berman has said Jackson was the last of seven candidates ESPN interviewed for the analyst seat. The two reunited in 2019 for a digital-only version of the show.

Funeral or memorial plans had not been announced as of Sunday afternoon. Expect tributes from the Broncos and from ESPN's NFL programming in the coming days.

faq.a: Neither his family, ESPN nor the Broncos has disclosed a cause of death. Chris Berman called it unexpected.

faq.q: When did Tom Jackson work at ESPN?
faq.a: From 1987 until his retirement in 2016, mostly on "NFL PrimeTime" and "Sunday NFL Countdown" with Chris Berman. He returned with Berman in 2019 for a digital version of "PrimeTime."

faq.q: Is Tom Jackson in the Hall of Fame?
faq.a: Not as a player. He received the Pro Football Hall of Fame's Pete Rozelle Radio-Television Award for broadcasting in 2015 and is in the Broncos Ring of Fame (1992).
He was 75. He was born April 4, 1951, in Cleveland.
